subject: Archaeology
title: Zooarchaeology: Reading Animal Bones
description: Learn Zooarchaeology: Reading Animal Bones in one minute.

hook.text: The animal bones in ancient trash heaps reveal what people ate, what they farmed, and how they treated their animals.

buildup.text: Zooarchaeologists identify species, age at death, butchery marks, and signs of disease from bone fragments.

discovery.text: Domesticated animals have smaller bones than wild ancestors. Tracking size changes reveals when domestication happened.

twist.text: Cut marks on human bones at some sites reveal cannibalism. Animal bone experts are often the ones who spot the evidence.

climax.text: At Jamestown colony, horse and dog bones show butchery marks — proof the settlers ate their animals during the starving time.

punchline.text: Trash tells the truth. What people threw away reveals what they could not admit.

quiz.question: How do zooarchaeologists detect animal domestication?
options: Domesticated animals have different colored bones
Domesticated animals have smaller bones than their wild ancestors
Domesticated animals are always found inside structures
